title: Palindromic Substrings
description: Given a string `s`, count how many of its substrings are palindromes. Substrings that sit at different positions are counted separately even when their text is identical.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Testing every substring costs O(n^3). Can you instead enumerate palindromes by where they are centred?
Each palindrome has exactly one centre: a character or a gap between two characters.
Expand from every centre while the ends match, and add one to the total for each successful expansion.

solution.explanation: Every palindrome is determined by its centre, and there are 2n-1 centres. From each one expand outwards while the end characters are equal; each step that succeeds corresponds to one more palindromic substring. Total work is O(n^2) time with O(1) space. For all-equal strings the answer is n(n+1)/2.
